s:
In the context of the enactment of Budget, which of the following statement / statements is / are valid?
I. The Appropriation Bill carries an automatic repeal clause.
II. The provision ' Vote on Account ' has become ineffectual after the re-scheduling of the budget cycle from the last day of February to the first day of February.
III. Amendments to either reject or reduce a tax can not be moved in case of the Finance Bill.
IV. The expenditure charged on the Consolidated 47. Fund of India can only be discussed.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: I is correct – since the Appropriation Act, 2016 Appropriation Acts carry an automatic repeal (sunset) clause; IV is correct – charged expenditure is only discussed. II is wrong (vote on account is still used in election years) and III is wrong (amendments to reduce or abolish a tax can be moved to the Finance Bill).
flag: | A vote on account is still used, mainly in election years with an interim budget.

s: If a party has 100 legislators (MLAs) in an assembly, as per anti-defection law, how many members are required to create a break-away faction without attracting disqualification?
o: None – no split is protected since 2003 (only a merger by 67 escapes)
src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (None – no split is protected since 2003 (only a merger by 67 escapes)); it is added as option 5.
the one-third split exception (34 of 100) was deleted by the 91st Amendment, 2003 — now no split is protected; only a two-thirds merger (67 of 100) escapes (Rocket Polity #77)
Since the 91st Amendment (2003) deleted the one-third split exception, no break-away faction of any size escapes disqualification; only a merger backed by two-thirds (67 of 100) is protected. 34 (one-third) was the answer under the pre-2003 law, and 30, 33 and 35 were never right.
flag: Printed options assume the pre-2003 law (key 34); option e was added for current law. | 34 (one-third) was protected only before the 91st Amendment (2003).

s: Which of the following statements is correct about the Anti-Defection Law?
o: The Anti-Defection Law protects members from disqualification in cases where one-third of the members of a legislative party split to form a new group.
A person disqualified on the grounds of defection can become a Minister if he belongs to the ruling party.

If a nominated member fails to join a political party within 6 months of commencement of his term, it is considered as grounds for disqualification of the member of a House of the State Legislature under the Tenth schedule of the constitution.
Disqualification on the grounds of defection does not apply when a member goes out of his party as a result of a merger of the party with another party.
src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
x: Disqualification does not apply when a member goes out of his party as a result of a merger (Para 4). The one-third split exception was deleted in 2003; a disqualified defector cannot become a Minister till re-elected (Art. 75(1B)/164(1B)); a nominated member is disqualified only if he joins a party after six months, not for failing to join.
flag: | The split exception was deleted by the 91st Amendment (2003).

s: Regarding anti defection, which of the following is not correct?
o: If a member defects from one party to some other party he is disqualified by the speaker
If a party expels an elected member of the party, the Member does not lose his seat in Legislature immediately
If a group of one-Third of members of the party decided to split, they will not lose their seats
If a group of 2/3 of the total members of a party decide to merge with some other party
src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains
x: Since the 91st Amendment (2003) a one-third split no longer protects members, so that statement is not correct. A defector is disqualified by the Speaker, an expelled member keeps his seat, and a two-thirds merger is protected.
flag: Option d is an incomplete sentence; read as the merger exception. | The one-third split exception was deleted in 2003; such members are disqualified.

s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about the Governor?

a. He can nominate one member to the state legislature assembly from the Anglo Indian Community.

b. He can seek any information relating to the administration of the affairs of the state and proposals for legislation from the Chief Minister.

c. A person completed the age of 30 can be appointed as governor.

d. The governor acts as agent of the central government.
x:
Anglo-Indian nomination to State Assemblies (Art. 333) ended on 25 January 2020 under the 104th Amendment — now only (b) is correct (Constitution (104th Amendment) Act, 2019)
In 2019 (a) and (b) were correct: the Governor nominated one Anglo-Indian to the Assembly (Art. 333) (now ended – 25 Jan 2020, 104th Amendment) and can seek information from the CM (Art. 167). The minimum age is 35, not 30, and he is constitutionally not an agent of the Centre.

s:
Identify the correct statement/statements with regard to Jammu and Kashmir

A. Governor's Rule is possible in Jammu And Kashmir

B. President's Rule can be imposed in Jammu and kashmir under the article 356 of the Indian Constitution

C. Financial Emergency cannot be imposed in Jammu and kashmir under the article 360 of the Indian Constitution

D. Right to Property is still a fundamental right in Jammu & Kashmir.
x:
Art. 370 was made inoperative and J&K became a UT on 31 Oct 2019 (J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019) — now none of A-D holds; President's Rule there is under Sec. 73 of that Act (indiacode.nic.in)
In 2019, before the August 2019 changes, all four were true for J&K: Governor's Rule under Sec. 92 of the J&K Constitution, Art. 356 thereafter, Art. 360 not applicable, and the right to property still a FR there.
